title: Any two edges of a block lie on a common cycle
statement: Let $G$ be a finite block — a connected graph with no cut vertex — on at least three vertices. Then any two distinct edges $e_1$ and $e_2$ of $G$ lie on a common cycle; that is, there is a cycle in $G$ whose edge set contains both $e_1$ and $e_2$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a block (connected, no cut vertex)
e_1 and e_2 are edges of G
replaced:
If $G$ is a block with $\nu \geq 3$, then any two edges of
$G$ lie on a common cycle.
